recall_prompt: Say how you would prove this — name each move in order.

steps.label: Write both as fractions
steps.margin_note: First mark. Same opening as the twin — reduce everything to sine and cosine.
steps.memory_tip: Reduce everything to sine and cosine first.

recall.must_convey: That cotA and tanA are written as cosA/sinA and sinA/cosA.
accept: write cot A as cos A over sin A and tan A as sin A over cos A
express both in sine and cosine
convert cot and tan into fractions
cot A ni cos A by sin A ga rasta
put both over sine and cosine

steps.why: Identical first move to the twin. What changes is the sign between them, and everything downstream follows from that.
common_mistakes: Writing tan A as cos A / sin A.

steps.label: Subtract over a common denominator
steps.margin_note: Second mark. The numerator is cos²A − sin²A — a DIFFERENCE this time, and that is exactly cos 2A.
steps.memory_tip: The numerator is cos²A − sin²A, a DIFFERENCE — and that is exactly cos 2A.

recall.must_convey: That subtracting gives cos²A − sin²A on top, which is cos 2A.
accept: the numerator is cos squared minus sin squared which is cos two A
subtracting gives a difference of squares equal to cos two A
combine and the top becomes cos two A
numerator cos square minus sin square ante cos two A
the difference gives cos two A

steps.why: A sum of the squares gives 1; a DIFFERENCE gives cos 2A. That single change is what separates this proof from its twin.
common_mistakes: Getting sin²A − cos²A and picking up a sign.

steps.label: Introduce the double angle
steps.margin_note: Third mark. Same trick as the twin — double top and bottom so the denominator becomes sin 2A.
steps.memory_tip: Double top and bottom so the denominator becomes sin 2A.

recall.must_convey: That top and bottom are doubled so the denominator becomes sin 2A.
accept: multiply top and bottom by two so the bottom is sin two A
introduce the double angle in the denominator
double both to get two cos two A over sin two A
rendu vaipula two tho multiply cheyyali
the denominator becomes sin two A

steps.why: Both this proof and its twin need the same 2 manufactured in the denominator. Only the numerator differs.
common_mistakes: Doubling only one side of the fraction.

steps.label: Convert to cot
steps.margin_note: Last mark. cos over sin is cot, so the answer is 2 cot 2A.
steps.memory_tip: cos over sin is cot, so the answer is 2 cot 2A.

recall.must_convey: That cos 2A / sin 2A is written as cot 2A, giving 2 cot 2A.
accept: cos two A over sin two A is cot two A so the answer is two cot two A
the ratio is cot so it becomes two cot two A
convert to cot to finish
cos by sin ante cot, so two cot two A
the answer is two cot two A

steps.why: The twin ended in cosec because its numerator was 1; this one ends in cot because its numerator is a cosine.
common_mistakes: Leaving the answer as a fraction.

insider_note: Write both as fractions over sinA cosA, and the numerator becomes cos2A directly. Doubling top and bottom is what turns sinA cosA into sin2A.
